text: Thinking about your most recent 20 competitive serves, approximately how many landed in the correct service box?
help: Use recent games against similar-level opponents. Do not use a cooperative serving drill.

text: Of your most recent 10 successful serves, how many landed in the back third of the service box?
help: Count only serves that landed in. The back third means reasonably close to the baseline, not merely past halfway.

text: In a 10-serve target test, how many times can you hit the called forehand, backhand or body third without faulting?
help: Choose the target before serving and alternate targets. A broad third of the service box counts.

text: Thinking about your most recent 20 competitive returns, approximately how many landed in?
help: Count return faults and returns hit long or wide as misses.

text: Of your most recent 10 successful returns, how many landed in the back third of the court?
help: Count controlled depth, even if the return was not hit hard.

text: After your most recent 10 returns, how many times did you reach the kitchen line balanced before the opponent contacted the third shot?
help: Do not count arrivals where you were still running, drifting or unable to split-step.

text: Of your most recent 20 third-shot drop attempts, how many landed in the kitchen and prevented an immediate downward attack?
help: Count a drop only when it gave your team a realistic chance to advance. A high ball that was smashed does not count.

text: Of your most recent 10 forehand third-shot drops in games, how many were low enough to prevent an immediate downward attack?
help: Use match attempts from the baseline or deep transition area.

text: Of your most recent 10 backhand third-shot drops in games, how many were low enough to prevent an immediate downward attack?
help: Include straight and cross-court attempts. Estimate from fewer attempts only when necessary.

text: When the return is unusually deep, short, fast or angled, what happens to your next drop attempt most often?
help: Choose the description that best matches recent competitive games.

options.text: I usually use the same swing and frequently miss or leave the ball high
I recognise the different return, but my adjustment is usually late or unreliable
I can adjust successfully when the change is obvious and I am balanced
I usually adjust arc, pace and target while keeping the ball difficult to attack
I consistently adapt from either wing and still control the following transition ball

text: Which statement best describes how you choose between a third-shot drive and drop?
help: Base your answer on return height and depth, your balance, opponent position and the fifth shot you expect.

options.text: I normally use my preferred shot regardless of the return
I consider the return, but often choose a shot that puts us under pressure
I make the correct choice on clear, comfortable returns
I usually choose correctly across deep, short, high and angled returns
I deliberately combine drives, drops and planned fifth shots to exploit opponent positioning

text: After your most recent 10 usable third-shot drops, how many times did you control the next ball and continue moving forward?
help: Count a repetition only when the fifth shot stayed low enough for your team to keep transitioning.

text: In competitive cross-court dink rallies, how many neutral or purposeful dinks can you usually play before your first unforced error or attackable pop-up?
help: Use rallies against an opponent who changes depth and placement, not cooperative straight feeds.

options.text: 15 or more while still changing placement deliberately

text: Of your most recent 10 straight-ahead dinks, how many stayed low enough that the opponent could not attack downward?
help: Straight dinks have less court length, so count both net errors and high pop-ups as unsuccessful.

text: During a normal dink rally, which description best matches how you create openings?
help: Consider whether your placement has a purpose and whether you can build more than one shot.

options.text: I mainly try to keep the ball in play and rarely select a target
I occasionally aim wide or at a backhand, but cannot repeat the placement
I can use one purposeful placement when I receive a comfortable ball
I regularly combine depth, width and middle targets to move an opponent
I build multi-shot patterns, recognise the opponent's adjustment and change the next target

text: Of your most recent 10 dinks played while an opponent was changing pace, depth or direction, how many remained controlled and unattackable?
help: Do not use cooperative warm-up dinks.

text: Of the last 10 kitchen balls you contacted clearly below net height, how many did you keep neutral instead of attempting a low-percentage attack?
help: A neutral dink, reset or controlled roll that did not give away an attack counts.

text: After reaching for 10 wide dinks, how many times can you recover to a balanced kitchen position before the opponent's next contact?
help: Count both the quality of your shot and your ability to recover without crossing your feet or leaving a large gap.

text: Of your most recent 10 low balls received in the transition zone, how many did you reset into the kitchen without leaving an easy attack?
help: Count blocks or soft resets. Drives from below net height that left your team under pressure do not count.

text: Of the last 10 hard drives you received at the kitchen, how many did you block back low enough to avoid an immediate second attack?
help: A ball that stays in but sits high should not be counted as successful.

text: Of the last 10 fast balls directed at your body or backhand side, how many did you block back low and controlled?
help: Use compact defensive contacts rather than full counterattacks.

text: After your team left the ball attackable, how many of the last 10 opponent attacks did you defend well enough to remain neutral or stay in the rally?
help: Count successful blocks, digs and resets. Merely touching the ball does not count.

text: Of your most recent 10 intentional defensive lobs, how many cleared the opponent and landed in without creating an easy overhead?
help: Use only deliberate lobs from pressure situations. Choose the first answer if you do not intentionally use this shot.

options.text: I do not use this shot, or 0–2 succeeded

text: In your most recent 10 fast hands exchanges, how many times did you control at least two consecutive contacts or finish the exchange positively?
help: This measures recovery after the first difficult ball, not only the opening counter.

text: Which statement best describes the balls you choose to speed up from the kitchen?
help: Consider contact height, your balance, disguise, target and the counter you expect.

options.text: I speed up mainly because I want to attack, even when the ball is low
I recognise obvious high balls but also attack many neutral or poorly balanced balls
I usually attack clear opportunities and keep most low balls neutral
I create or recognise smaller openings and usually choose a suitable target
I disguise attacks, anticipate the counter and vary patterns based on opponent reactions

text: Of your most recent 10 kitchen speed-ups, how many created a weak reply, won the rally or led to a favourable counter exchange?
help: Do not count attacks that went out, into the net or directly into an opponent's preferred counter.

text: Of the last 10 attackable balls you countered on your forehand side, how many stayed in and created at least a neutral outcome?
help: A neutral outcome means you did not immediately lose the advantage or pop the ball up.

text: Of the last 10 attackable balls you countered on your backhand or body side, how many stayed in and created at least a neutral outcome?
help: Include compact counters during fast kitchen exchanges.

text: Which statement best describes your target selection when attacking from the kitchen?
help: Examples include the dominant hip, paddle-side shoulder, middle gap or open court.

options.text: I mainly hit hard at the opponent without selecting a target
I know useful targets but rarely control the ball well enough to use them
I can target an obvious body or middle gap on comfortable balls
I regularly match my target to the opponent's position and paddle preparation
I disguise and vary targets to create predictable counters for the next ball

text: Across your most recent 10 points containing side-to-side or forward movement, how many times did you stay connected to your partner without leaving a large gap?
help: Count the whole point, including transition movement and recovery after wide balls.

text: In your most recent 10 balls through the middle, how many were handled cleanly without hesitation, collision or both players abandoning the ball?
help: Use normal partner communication and court responsibilities.

text: Which statement best describes how you use an opponent's weaker wing, movement or recurring error?
help: Good targeting includes noticing when the opponent adjusts and avoiding becoming completely predictable.

options.text: I rarely identify a specific weakness during the match
I notice a weakness late but struggle to direct enough balls toward it
I can identify and use one obvious weakness
I test several weaknesses and change the pattern when the opponent adjusts
I build points that expose a weakness while mixing targets enough to remain unpredictable

text: When an opponent repeats the same speed-up, return or movement pattern, when do you normally recognise it?
help: Choose what happens in real matches, not what you believe you should notice.

options.text: I usually do not recognise the pattern during the match
I recognise it only after many points or when a partner mentions it
I recognise an obvious pattern after it happens several times
I recognise it early enough to change positioning or shot selection
I test the pattern, anticipate it and adjust again when the opponent changes

text: In your most recent 10 extended neutral rallies, how many times did you avoid forcing an attack before a clearly favourable ball appeared?
help: Count patient point construction, not passive dinking with no purpose.

text: In your most recent 10 close-score points at 8–8 or later, how many times did you execute your normal first three contacts without an unforced error?
help: Use tournament games or competitive rec play. Estimate from similar pressure points when necessary.

text: In a typical game to 11, approximately how many points end because of your unforced error before the opponents create strong pressure?
help: Examples include missed serves, missed returns, routine balls in the net and avoidable balls hit long.

text: On a below-average playing day, which parts of your game normally remain dependable?
help: Choose your performance floor, not the worst game you have ever played.

options.text: Even serves, returns and routine balls become unreliable
Serves and returns remain usable, but most rally skills break down
My basic game remains usable, but pressure exposes several weaknesses
Most core shots and decisions remain reliable despite reduced quality
My consistency and decisions change only slightly from a normal day

text: After two or three similar errors in a game, what do you normally do during the next few points?
help: Think about a recent match where one shot or pattern repeatedly failed.

options.text: I repeat the same choice or become more aggressive without a clear change
I know something is wrong but usually adjust only after several more errors
I make one basic change such as adding margin or choosing a safer target
I identify the likely cause and adjust pace, target, technique or shot selection
I make a specific adjustment quickly, evaluate it and make a second change if needed

text: Against established 3.5 players, in how many of your most recent 10 games did your own play remain competitive rather than being consistently targeted or protected?
help: Count your contribution to rallies and decisions, not only whether your team won.

text: Against established 4.0 players, in how many of your most recent 10 games could you sustain neutral rallies without opponents consistently exposing you?
help: Use direct experience. Choose the first option if you have not yet played enough established 4.0 opponents.

options.text: No useful sample, or 0–1 out of 10

text: When partnered with a clearly stronger player, which description best matches your contribution?
help: Consider returns, transitions, defence, neutral rallies and whether opponents can repeatedly isolate you.

options.text: My partner must cover unusually much of the court and construct most points
I contribute occasionally, but opponents can repeatedly target me for an advantage
I hold my position in routine rallies but create few advantages
I contribute consistently, defend my space and help create attacking opportunities
I function as an equal partner and remain effective when opponents deliberately target me

text: Across your first two games with an unfamiliar partner, which description most often fits your performance?
help: Consider communication, spacing, middle responsibility and your ability to play without rehearsed patterns.

options.text: My positioning and decisions usually break down badly
I need several games before I stop leaving major gaps or causing confusion
I can play a functional basic game after a short adjustment
I normally communicate and adapt within the first game
I quickly identify our strengths, organise responsibilities and play close to my normal level

text: Compared with your normal competitive recreational level, how does your tournament or high-pressure performance usually change?
help: Use organised league, ladder or elimination games when you do not have tournament experience.

options.text: It drops by roughly a full level or my basic skills regularly fail
It drops noticeably and several normal strengths become unreliable
It drops slightly, especially early or in close-score situations
It stays close to my normal level
It stays fully reliable or improves under pressure
